newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Dec electric futures settle near record high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Dec electric futures settle near record high.

text.p: NYMEX December electricity futures settled Wednesday near all-time record highs on strong spot power demand in the Pacific Northwest and impressive rally in the domestic and Canadian natural gas prices.
"You'll see it continue to go higher. I think it's just speculation where gas is going to go," a Houston trader.
Chilly weather in the Northwest following the region's first snow storm earlier this week pushed up power and natgas demand for space-heating.
December natural gas prices at the San Juan/Blanco Hub ended near $3.59 per million British thermal units, up sharply from Tuesday's $2.72-$2.73.
Spot cash power prices in the western U.S. were also spurred by tight electricity supplies amid outages of several coal-fired generating units in the region.
Most of those units were shut last week, and scheduled to return to service this week.
In the Northwest, the 700 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired station was scheduled to restart Thursday.

In the Southwest, the 790 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired complex near Laughlin, Nev., returned to service today, but its output were reduced to 670 MW due to a mill fire. Restart of the 220 MW unit 3 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in Arizona was uncertain after being shut November 8 due to a bolier tube leak.
December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures, after posting an all-time record high of $30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), settled at $29.73, up $2.48 from Tuesday's close.
January 1997 COB futures finished at its new life-of-contract high at $25.75, up $2.08 from Tuesday. Deferred COB ended 30 cents to $1.72 higher.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures set a new contract high at $29.80, near the record high of $30.00. The spot PV contract ended at $29.40, up $3.98.
January 1997 PV finished up $2.78 at $25.18 after posting a new contract high at $25.25. Outer-month PVs ended 50 cents to $2.25 higher.
Most brokers and traders expect the electricity complex to scale new heights if natural gas continues to post new highs. The December electricity contracts will expire Friday.
According to latest forecasts, the Northwest was expected to receive temperatures four to eight degrees below normal, and Southwest slightly above normal temperatures for the rest of the week.
NYMEX estimated 269 COB and 221 PV contracts were sold.
